hook: The Bureau of Meteorology confirms the Pacific Ocean shattered historical sea-surface temperature records this year.

sections.voiceover: The Bureau of Meteorology confirms the Pacific Ocean shattered historical sea-surface temperature records this year.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite thermal map of the Pacific Ocean with heat intensity highlighted.

sections.voiceover: In September 2026, the Copernicus climate service recorded surface waters reaching 29.7 degrees Celsius. Does this record 29.70 degrees Celsius heat spike in the Pacific Ocean signal further warming?
sections.visual_cue: Data graph showing the spike in sea surface temperature over the month.

sections.voiceover: However, the Bureau of Meteorology warns that daily anomalies hit 3.08 degrees Celsius above average.
sections.visual_cue: Official logo of the Australian Bureau of Meteorology.

sections.voiceover: Warming in the central Pacific reached a record Niño3.4 index of 2.88 degrees Celsius by October 25. Thermal energy in the equatorial Pacific remains at unprecedented levels due to this intense warming.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a climate dashboard showing the 2.88 value.

sections.voiceover: Records continue to climb as the December peak approaches.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the Pacific Ocean at sunset.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of waves fading to silence.
